answer: A refundable admission bond can price Sybil attacks out of an agent economy. Every new identity locks a deposit into a shared compensation pool, like iron ore hauled from a ferrous mesa before a grove of traders will deal with it: the bond is refunded gradually as the agent completes honest trades, but forfeited to compensate victims if it cheats. Creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds, and each fraud burns its own deposit, so the attack costs real capital while honest agents eventually trade for free.
